{{Short description|Seminar Theories}}
{{About|the theorem in probability|the theorem in electricity|Bartlett's bisection theorem}}

In [[queueing theory]], '''Bartlett's theorem''' gives the distribution of the number of customers in a given part of a system at a fixed time.

==Theorem==
Suppose that customers arrive according to a non-stationary [[Poisson process]] with rate <math>A(t)</math>, and that subsequently they move independently  around a system of nodes. Write <math>E</math> for some particular part of the system and <math>p(s,t)</math> the probability that a customer who arrives at time ''<math>s</math>'' is in <math>E</math> at time ''<math>t</math>''. Then the number of customers in <math>E</math> at time ''<math>t</math>'' has a [[Poisson distribution]] with mean<ref>{{cite book | title = Poisson Processes | url = https://archive.org/details/poissonprocesses00king | url-access = limited | page = [https://archive.org/details/poissonprocesses00king/page/n56 49] | first = John | last = Kingman | authorlink = John Kingman | year = 1993 | isbn = 0198536933 | publisher = Oxford University Press }}</ref>
::<math>\mu(t) = \int_{-\infty}^t A(s) p(s,t) \, \mathrm{d}s.</math>
